title: Collateral Protection Insurance — Closing-Period Refund Check after Payoff of a Force-Placed Contract
content:
Collateral Protection Insurance refunds by check to the borrower the capitalised premium charge with the latest billing period start when its billing period runs past the closed date of a tracking record that closed while force-placed because its contract was paid off, and an accepted proof of the borrower's own coverage counts for that period. This rule governs that refund, the closing-period refund; it applies only on a tracking record on which no arrival channel holds more than one accepted proof-review entry.

## Conditions on the refund

The closing-period refund is fixed only after the records carry an accepted re-review of every rejected faxed proof whose shown coverage reaches into that billing period.

## Charges this rule does not fix

For the capitalised premium charge with the latest billing period start on a tracking record that closed while force-placed because its contract was paid off, when an accepted proof counts for that charge's period and no arrival channel holds more than one accepted proof-review entry on the record, the refund is fixed by the closing-month refund rule if the period ends on the closed date and by the closing-period refund rule if it runs past the closed date. That charge in any other case, and every other charge, keep the product's base refund rule in force:

- a premium charge can be refunded only once;
- when accepted proof shows coverage effective on or before the coverage effective date of the placed coverage with no gap, every premium charge of the placement is refunded in full (`full_no_lapse`);
- when accepted proof starts after the placed coverage's effective date, each unrefunded charge is refunded for the days of its billing period on or after the proof's policy effective date (`pro_rata_from_proof_effective`), and days before that date stay earned;
- when the record closes because the contract left active servicing while force-placed, each unrefunded charge is refunded for the days of its billing period after the contract's closed date (`pro_rata_from_closure`).

Where that latest charge stays under the base refund rule, the accepted proof the base rule reads is the record's accepted proof with the latest policy effective date, whatever its channel, and where two accepted proofs share that date the one recorded first counts. Its coverage is effective on or before the placed coverage's effective date with no gap when it took effect on or before the record's placement effective date and expires on or after it. The charge being refunded only once, when the proof clause and the closure clause both apply, it is refunded once for every day either clause gives, under `pro_rata_from_proof_effective` when the proof clause gives it a day and `pro_rata_from_closure` otherwise.

## Issuing the refund check: `mail_closing_period_refund_6483f0cd`

**Capability.** The borrower requests, on their own paid-off contract, the refund check for the one force-placed premium charge whose billing period was still running on the day their insurance tracking record closed. One call adds one premium-refund entry for that charge to the tracking record, dated today, with the amount and refund basis passed in, marked as mailed to the borrower by check at the mailing address on file, and lowers the tracking record's net premium total by that amount. No contract, deficiency or other account is touched.

**Invocation.** `mail_closing_period_refund_6483f0cd` is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `related_activity_id` | Id class: the reference number of the premium-charge entry being refunded, as returned by the tracking activity lookup. |
| `amount_usd` | Fixed-format class: the refund check amount in US dollars, a non-negative number with 2 decimal places (cents), rounded half-up to the cent. |
| `refund_basis` | Enum class: how the refunded days were determined, exactly one of the values below. |

Values of `refund_basis`:

- `full_no_lapse` — the borrower's own coverage ran with no gap from the coverage effective date of the placed coverage, so every day of the charge's period is refunded;
- `pro_rata_from_proof_effective` — the refund counts the days the borrower's accepted proof covers together with the other days the rule counts for it;
- `pro_rata_from_closure` — only the days of the period after the record's closed date are refunded;
- `held_premium_release` — reserved for releasing a premium held pending proof review, which never reached the contract;
- `not_applicable` — reserved for activity entries that are not refunds.

**Return.** A confirmation naming the new refund entry reference number, the premium charge refunded, the refund amount (USD, two decimals), the refund basis and destination, and the refund date (YYYY-MM-DD). The presence of the refund entry reference number indicates the check was issued, and the refund entry is then visible in the record's tracking activity.
